title: New Residential Construction (Census, October 2026 data — building permits, housing starts, completions) — the residential node's other leaf, same reference month as the 11-12 EHS print, 8:30 a.m. ET
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes), row "New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, and Housing Completions) | November 18, 2026 | 8:30 AM | October 2026", release code A202611180830, reference A202610. Corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (fetched direct 2026-09-06 from the live path www.atlantafed.org/-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/cqer/researchcq/gdpnow/ — the path every sibling ledger cites now 404s), whose 2026-11-18 row reads "Housing starts" at 0.35416666 of a day (08:30 ET). Filed `estimate` per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an in-sweep discovery, and doubly so because the same Census page demonstrably carries `Suspended` rows. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Why it earns its own row rather than a line in that ledger: it is the residential node's OTHER leaf, carrying the SAME reference month six days later. The Atlanta Fed's GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx Residential sheet routes `valExHomeSales` into `FRSBKX_USNAqtr` ("Brokerage commissions") for existing-home sales and `SplicedNewHousingConstruction` into `FRSPX_USNAqtr` ("Permanent-site" construction) — the far larger leaf — so October's existing and new residential activity can be read against each other rather than confused. Distinguishing features beyond routineness: it is 08:30, so unlike every 10:00 print in this corridor its surprise lands before the equity open; it shares its session with NAR's October Pending Home Sales Index at 10:00 and the FOMC minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting at 14:00 (fomc-minutes-2026-11-18, tracked); and it is the first single-release vintage after the 11-17 stack (retail sales + inventories, import/export prices, industrial production, MTIS). One question left explicitly open for its own initial research, because it is the mirror of what makes 11-12 clean: whether a 14:00 MINUTES release compresses the morning the way a 14:00 SEP decision does (the 12-09 ledger measured SPY's 10:00 hour at 26.0% of session range vs a 40.4% baseline on decision days) is UNMEASURED — this session did not test it and did not have an hourly bar source to test it with. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the inertness this session re-derived for the neighbouring EHS class (2,514 daily sessions 2016-09-06 -> 2026-09-04: 114 EHS release days leave ITB at 1.916% vs an 1.863% baseline, p=0.58); whether homebuilders are inert on a STARTS/PERMITS print is a separate question nobody here has measured, and it is the more plausible channel of the two. Distinct from the already-proposed housing-starts-2026-12-17, which is the NOVEMBER reference month and a funding-cliff test; this one is October's and a residential-channel test. One class considered and DECLINED so its absence reads as a decision: NAR's October Pending Home Sales Index on 2026-11-18, which the sibling lane already declined on the record as a routine monthly edition — the same criterion applies and nothing this session measured changes it. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
